2608.22462.title: Functional compatibility as a determinant of persistent neural learning
2608.22462.paper_summary: Artificial neural networks can acquire new capabilities but often damage existing ones when they continue to learn. This stability-plasticity problem has motivated replay, regularization and constrained-update methods, yet it remains unclear whether a property of incoming learning itself determines what can be retained without disrupting protected behaviour. Here we show that functional compatibility, the extent to which new learning can coexist with behaviour that must be preserved, is a causal determinant of persistent learning. To our knowledge, this is the first controlled causal demonstration in which compatibility is deliberately changed from matched neural states and persistent learning is measured under a common retention requirement. The effect generalizes across independent learning directions, convolutional and transformer architectures, vision and text, and additional seeds. Learning rules differ in how efficiently they exploit available compatibility, while retention constraints limit how much can be stored. At larger finite updates, nonlinear geometry changes the available learning opportunity and ultimately prevents the matched compatibility continuum from being realized. These results establish functional compatibility as an experimentally controllable principle of persistent neural learning, shifting the problem from preventing forgetting towards identifying which components of new learning can safely become permanent.
2608.22462.paper_summary_zh: 人工神經網絡可以獲得新的能力，但在持續學習時，往往會損害現有的能力。這種穩定性-可塑性問題促使了重播、正則化和受限更新方法的發展，但目前仍不清楚進來的學習本身的特性是否決定了什麼可以在不破壞受保護行為的情況下被保留。在這裡，我們展示了功能兼容性，即新學習與必須保留的行為共存的程度，是持續學習的因果決定因素。據我們所知，這是第一次在控制條件下的因果演示，其中兼容性是從匹配的神經狀態中故意改變的，並在共同的保留要求下測量持續學習。這一效應在獨立的學習方向、卷積和Transformer架構、視覺和文本以及其他種子中具有普遍性。學習規則在多大程度上有效利用可用的兼容性方面存在差異，而保留約束則限制了可以存儲的量。在較大的有限更新下，非線性幾何改變了可用的學習機會，最終阻止了匹配的兼容性連續體的實現。這些結果確立了功能兼容性作為持續神經學習的一個可實驗控制原則，將問題從防止遺忘轉向識別新學習中哪些組件可以安全地成為永久性。
2608.22462.author: Hossein Javidnia et.al.
